events.title: Nathan Hale Executed by the British
events.description: American Continental Army officer Nathan Hale was hanged by British forces in New York City after being captured while gathering intelligence behind enemy lines during the American Revolutionary War. He is traditionally credited with the last words, 'I only regret that I have but one life to lose for my country.'
events.significance: Hale became an enduring symbol of American patriotism and sacrifice, and is remembered as the first American spy hero of the Revolution.

events.title: U.S. Post Office Established
events.description: The Second Federal Congress passed legislation creating the office of Postmaster General, and the postal system was formalized under the new Constitution. Samuel Osgood was appointed as the first Postmaster General under the Constitution.
events.significance: This laid the foundation for the United States Postal Service, which became essential infrastructure for communication and commerce in the young nation.

events.title: Lincoln Issues the Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln issued the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation, declaring that enslaved people in Confederate states still in rebellion on January 1, 1863 would be free.
events.significance: It transformed the Civil War into a struggle against slavery, discouraged European intervention on behalf of the Confederacy, and paved the way for the abolition of slavery in the United States.

events.title: Iran-Iraq War Begins
events.description: Iraq launched a large-scale invasion of Iran, beginning a conflict that would last nearly eight years. Iraqi forces attacked Iranian air bases and advanced into Iranian territory, especially in Khuzestan.
events.significance: The war caused hundreds of thousands of deaths, devastated both economies, and had lasting effects on Middle Eastern geopolitics, ending in a stalemate in 1988.

events.title: Birth of the Modern Bulgarian Independence Anniversary Context: Bulgaria Declares Full Independence
events.description: On September 22, 1908, Bulgaria formally declared its full independence from the Ottoman Empire in the city of Veliko Tarnovo, with Prince Ferdinand proclaimed Tsar.
events.significance: The declaration ended Bulgaria's nominal vassalage to the Ottoman Empire and marked a key step in the Balkan political shifts preceding the Balkan Wars and World War I.
